text:
Harper Nguyen: hey team — Harper here, first day. Getting set up on a company-managed Windows laptop. Trying to follow the mac/linux bootstrap but running into friction: 

- I installed Chocolatey but the bootstrap uses asdf and expects a POSIX shell. Is it ok to use nvm for node on Windows?
- dotfiles bootstrap script tries to create symlinks but fails with 'Operation not permitted'
- ssh-agent: when I run `ssh-add` it says agent not found (I think corp policy changed ssh setup)

What do people do for parity across mac/linux/windows? Steps I ran: 
```
choco install git curl 7zip mingw -y
# cloned dotfiles into %USERPROFILE%\dotfiles and ran bootstrap.bat (it errors)
```

Maya (DevEx): welcome Harper! :wave: Short answers: we prefer asdf for cross-OS parity but on Windows folks do two things: use WSL2 as the primary dev shell, or use native tools with care. If you can run WSL2, that will match the onboarding docs closely. For a quick native approach: nvm is fine for node on Windows but we lose uniformity for CI and other runtimes. 

Jon (SRE): If you have WSL2 available on the corporate image, use it. Our dotfiles and CI expect POSIX paths and `~/.ssh`. WSL keeps everything simpler. If WSL is blocked, we support running the bootstrap under Git Bash / MSYS but you may hit symlink permissions due to Windows ACLs. 

Harper Nguyen: WSL2 isn't installed on this image (corporate lockdown). IT said I need a ticket for admin privileges. Any tips to make the symlinks work in native Windows? 

Maya (DevEx): For symlinks on native NTFS you need developer mode or admin rights to create symlinks. The bootstrap script can fallback to copying files instead of symlinking — edit `bootstrap.bat` or run the shell script under Git Bash and set `USE_COPY=1` env to force copies. Example: 
```
# in Git Bash
export USE_COPY=1
./bootstrap.sh
```
We also maintain `dotfiles/windows.md` with a copy-based alternative. 

Harper Nguyen: thanks — tried the copy fallback and it worked. Still missing ssh-agent though. `ssh-add` says agent not found in Git Bash. 

Jon (SRE): On corporate Windows we often use Pageant or the Windows OpenSSH agent. Try starting the OpenSSH auth agent service: 
```
# PowerShell (admin)
Start-Service ssh-agent
Get-Service ssh-agent
# then in Git Bash you might need to set SSH_AUTH_SOCK to the Windows pipe
export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/mnt/c/Users/Harper/AppData/Local/ssh-agent.sock # example
```
If that is hard, simplest route is to create a key inside your profile (`ssh-keygen -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa`) and add it to GitHub, then use `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa` in your shell after starting the appropriate agent. 

IT Support Bot: If you need admin to enable WSL2 or to configure ssh-agent service, file a request: https://internal.redwood.com/helpdesk — choose "Developer laptop admin". Include your asset tag. 

Harper Nguyen: I created a key inside Git Bash and added it to GH; cloning over SSH works now. Next step I'll file the helpdesk ticket for WSL2 so my environment matches Linux. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:
